description:
`jit --schema` emits its JSON with a different key order on each run, so two runs of the same binary produce different bytes. Deterministic output lets the machine contract be diffed, checksummed and committed as evidence.

## Background

Three consecutive runs of `jit --schema` on commit `b80e25ff2` produced three different SHA-256 digests while parsing to equal JSON values. The schema is assembled from hash-map-backed collections, so iteration order varies per process.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Repeated `jit --schema` runs of one binary produce byte-identical output.
- [hard] REQ-02: The ordering comes from the schema's own data structures (ordered maps or sorted keys at assembly), not from a post-serialization rewrite.
- [hard] REQ-03: One test owns the property by comparing two independently assembled schemas byte for byte.

## Notes

Surfaced at the close of the dispatch-layering epic and recorded there as a post-release follow-up; this issue is its tracked home.
title: Make jit --schema output byte-deterministic
